news_drafts.headline: Rhondda Cynon Taff gets clean audit but must fix vehicle disposal records
news_drafts.lead: Rhondda Cynon Taff Council has received an unqualified audit opinion on its 2025–26 accounts and will have them certified on 24 September, six days ahead of the statutory deadline. The Auditor General found the council produced "a high-quality set of accounts" and identified no material uncertainties about its ability to continue as a going concern. However, auditors identified a material control weakness: £1.4m of fully depreciated vehicles remain recorded on the asset register despite having been disposed of. The audit report states that "a material population of fully depreciated vehicles remain recorded in the register," indicating the council's vehicle disposal and asset register review processes are "not operating effectively." The council corrected all material misstatements totalling £10.5m before finalisation.

news_drafts.headline: Rhondda Cynon Taff council warns service cuts are 'highly likely' as £59m shortfall looms
news_drafts.lead: Rhondda Cynon Taff council must find £59.2m over three years from 2027/28 to 2029/30 to balance its budget, the cabinet heard on 21 September. The council warned that revisions to service delivery arrangements and associated staffing levels are "highly likely" as a result. This follows three consecutive years of deficits each exceeding £30m and a current-year shortfall of more than £20m. The council's analysis shows that even using reserves — money a council has set aside — to cover the shortfall would require over £150m, and would still leave a £73m permanent reduction in its base budget, signalling that permanent service cuts rather than temporary borrowing must be the main mechanism for addressing the problem.

news_drafts.headline: Rhondda Cynon Taff warns of service cuts as three-year budget gap reaches £59.2m
news_drafts.lead: Rhondda Cynon Taff Council faces a cumulative budget gap — the difference between planned spending and expected income — of £59.2 million across the next three years, following annual shortfalls above £20 million in the current year and above £30 million in each of the three years before. The council has warned that service delivery changes and staffing cuts are "highly likely". Even using £150 million in reserves, money the council has put aside, would not close the gap; the council would still need permanent spending cuts of £73 million by the end of the planning period. The deficit is highly sensitive to funding from Welsh Government: a one percentage point change in annual funding creates a £5.6 million swing in budget pressure across the three years. The council is modelling council tax increases of 3 per cent a year to contribute £4.5 million to £4.7 million towards closing the gap.

findings.headline: Settlement funding sensitivity creates £35M variance in three-year budget gap between optimistic and pessimistic scenarios.
findings.detail: The council's budget is highly sensitive to Welsh Government settlement levels, with each 1% change impacting the budget gap by £5.6M annually. Modelling ranges from +3% growth (three-year gap of £55.4M) to +1% growth (three-year gap of £90.1M), a swing of £34.7M. This means the final funding requirement is substantially determined by political funding decisions outside the council's control.
findings.matters: High sensitivity to external funding creates forecast uncertainty; councils dependent on volatile funding streams face difficulty planning, and lenders have reduced visibility of actual outturn until settlements are confirmed.
findings.figures: Sensitivity analysis shows £5.6M impact per 1% change in settlement (section 6.1); Figure 1 base-case scenarios show 3-year gap of £55,409k (at +3% WG resource) vs £90,144k (at +1% WG resource)
findings.quote: The variability of the potential level of the Settlement from Welsh Government has a significant impact on the budget gap, at £5.6M per 1%

findings.headline: Council anticipates significant service reductions and workforce changes to close the budget gap.
findings.detail: The council states it is "highly likely that revisions to some service delivery arrangements will be required and associated staffing levels." While services will be protected "wherever possible," the scale of the gap requires changes to delivery models and staffing. Service-level reductions are listed as "a last resort" but are acknowledged as likely given the sustained significant budget gaps.
findings.matters: Service reductions and workforce cuts signal deteriorating service capacity; councils making large cuts face operational risk and may struggle to meet statutory obligations in areas like social care, affecting their creditworthiness.
findings.figures: £36.9M Additional Budget Requirement in 2027/28 alone; three-year cumulative additional requirement £107.0M (Figure 1)
findings.quote: it is highly likely that revisions to some service delivery arrangements will be required and associated staffing levels, based on the continued significant budget gaps which we face

findings.headline: Reserves inadequate to bridge structural deficit; £150M+ depletion still leaves £73M of permanent budget cuts needed.
findings.detail: The council's Medium-Term Financial Plan shows that using reserves alone to balance the budget would require over £150M of draw-downs over the three-year period, yet the council would still require approximately £73M of permanent base-budget reductions by the end of the planning period. This demonstrates reserves cannot sustainably address the structural deficit.
findings.matters: Reserves depletion signals weakening financial resilience; simultaneous reserve exhaustion and base-budget cuts indicate the council has limited tools left to manage the deficit, creating acute liquidity pressure.
findings.figures: £150M+ reserves required; £73M permanent base-budget cuts still needed despite reserve depletion (section 8.3); base-case 3-year budget gap £72,947k (Figure 1)
findings.quote: to balance the budget (base case) using reserves alone would require the use of over £150M of reserves and the Council would still have a need to reduce its base budget by approximately £73M at the end of this period

findings.headline: Council faces £25.7M budget gap in 2027/28 in a multi-year structural deficit.
findings.detail: The council is modelling a base-case budget gap of £25.7M for 2027/28 (before Council Tax increases), followed by gaps of £25.6M and £21.7M in subsequent years, totalling £72.9M over three years at 2% Welsh Government settlement growth. This follows a pattern of gaps exceeding £20M in the current year and £30M+ in each of the three years prior.
findings.matters: A council with consistent multi-year deficits of this scale faces ongoing risk to service delivery and financial sustainability; lenders assessing creditworthiness need to understand capacity to manage borrowing alongside structural imbalance.
findings.figures: 2027/28: £25.7M (section 7.2); 3-year total £72,947k (Figure 1); current year gap exceeds £20M; preceding three years exceeded £30M each (section 4.4)
findings.quote: the Council facing a budget gap of £25.7M (before any increase in Council Tax) for the next financial year and follows on from the significant gaps in previous years

findings.paper_title: Report of the Deputy Chief Executive & Group Director of Corporate Resources
findings.headline: The council missed the statutory 31st May deadline for certifying draft accounts
findings.detail: Section 3.2 requires draft accounts to be certified by 31st May under the Accounts and Audit (Wales) Regulations. Section 3.3 confirms RCT certified draft accounts on 30th June 2026, one month late. Section 3.2 states that when deadlines are missed, councils must publish a statement setting out reasons for non-compliance; the paper confirms appropriate notices were published on the council website.
findings.matters: Missing statutory deadlines can indicate resource constraints or process issues in financial management, signalling potential governance weaknesses
findings.figures: 31st May statutory deadline; draft accounts certified 30th June 2026
findings.quote: If these timescales are not met then there is a requirement to publish a statement setting out the reasons for non-compliance. In accordance with these requirements, appropriate notices were published on the Council website.
